safety_lead_time.comparison_action: DECREASE safety lead time from 5.0 to 2.87 days; safety stock buffer is more effective for this lumpy demand pattern

narrative: Material PL1__M8AEE259 exhibits lumpy demand (CV=1.21) across 95 working-day observations from March 2025 to March 2026, with 29.5% zero-demand days and occasional peaks above 2,200 units. Lead times average 2.69 working days with moderate variability (CV=0.40), dominated by transport uncertainty (60% of variance). The current SAP safety stock of 0 units is critically insufficient for the 95% service level target; the recommended (r,Q) policy lifts safety stock to 1,516 units with a reorder point of 2,937 units and an EOQ-driven order quantity of 45,564 units, achieving the target at a total annual cost of approximately $449.
warnings: SAP safety stock is 0 — current ERP policy provides no demand buffer and will result in frequent stockouts.
Two high-demand outliers detected (>2,200 units) — winsorisation applied at upper fence.
Safety lead time reduced from SAP 5.0 days to model-recommended 2.87 days; explicit safety stock buffer is preferred for lumpy demand.

research_insights.selected_model: (r,Q) — Continuous-review Reorder Point / Fixed Order Quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Lumpy demand with moderate lead time variability is best managed under continuous review; the (r,Q) policy triggers a fixed replenishment of 45,564 units whenever stock falls to the reorder point of 2,937 units, balancing ordering and holding costs via EOQ while the safety stock absorbs demand and lead time uncertainty. The MOQ of 559 is non-binding as EOQ greatly exceeds it.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Safety stock (1,516) plus order quantity (45,564) totals 47,080 units, well within the 160,799-unit storage limit. No capacity constraint binds; full policy is feasible.
